newsitem.title: USA: Bankers Trust Q1 net chargeoffs $15 mln.
newsitem.headline: Bankers Trust Q1 net chargeoffs $15 mln.

text.p: Bankers Trust New York Corp said net chargeoffs in the first quarter of 1997 totaled $15 million versus $10 million a year ago.
Cash basis loans declined to $332 million at the end of the first quarter of 1997 from $715 million a year ago and $452 million at the end of the fourth quarter of 1996.

Bankers Trust said the decline in the first quarter was attributable to collections of $69 million, chargeoffs of $33 million and sales of existing cash basis loans of $31 million. These decreases were slightly offset by additional transfers to cash basis loans of $16 million.
Bankers Trust said there was no provision for credit losses in the first quarter compared with a $5 million provision in the first quarter of 1996.

Investment banking had net income of $96 milliion compard with $82 million a year ago, reflecting higher corproate finance fees and net revenue from equity trnaactions. Net revenues in investment banking rose to $303 million from $227 million a year ago.

In trading and sales, net income rose to $43 million from $24 million a year ago. Bankers Trust said the improvement was due to higher revenues from trading and client-related business. Net revneue in trading and sales rose to $134 million from $90 million a year ago.

Risk Management Services recorded net income of $11 million in the first quarter of 1997, compared to a $4 million loss in the first quarter of 1996. Revenues of $105 million rose from $63 million a year ago. Compared to the prior year period, revenues from new derivatives transactions and from the Emerging Europe, Middle East and Africa unit improved.
Bankers Trust said total non-interest expenses of $935 million increased by $174 million, or 23 percent, from the first quarter of 1996.
Salaries expense increased $36 million, or 18 percent, principally due to an eight percent increase in the average number of employees and to merit increases.

Incentive compensation and employee benefits, the largest component of non-interest expenses, increased $95 million due to higher earnings, greater emphasis on performance-based compensation and the increase in the average number of employees, the company said.
